newsitem.title: USA: Good news outweighs bad in D.C. budget - D.C. CFO.
newsitem.headline: Good news outweighs bad in D.C. budget - D.C. CFO.

text.p: While the District of Columbia's 1998 budget process contains good news and bad, good news accounts for 95 percent of the picture, Anthony Williams, D.C.'s Chief Financial Officer, said Wednesday.

"The bad news is that the control board and the District couldn't agree on a budget, and now they are sending two budgets up to the Congress for consideration," Williams, a speaker The Bond Buyer's Investor Forum here, said. "The 95 percent good news is...that out of these $5 billion-dollar-odd budgets, there is essentially 99 percent agreement between all of the parties."
Disagreement over about $6 million to $10 million of expenditures separates the sides, he said.
"That's very, very good news," Williams said.
Further good news is that everyone agreed to balance the budget a year early, and, after some initial problems, to essentially balance it without resorting to any gimmicks, he said.
"We've been very, very conservative about revenue estimation, and we are doing everything we can to remain as conservative as possible in terms of expenditure estimation," Williams said.
